audit_findings.title: Unaccrued Eaton Fire losses could consume common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecovered claims, legal costs, penalties, restitution and financing costs would reduce future OE or require a direct equity-value bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: In light of pending litigation, it is probable that Edison International and SCE will incur additional material losses in connection with the Eaton Fire.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that additional material Eaton losses are probable, but it cannot estimate their range. The amount ultimately borne by shareholders after customer, Wildfire Fund, insurance and third-party recoveries is unresolved. Because the valuation contains no allowance for that net leakage, the exposure is reasonably capable of reducing every scenario materially.
audit_findings.action: Build probability-weighted and severe downside stresses for total Eaton claims, legal costs, penalties, restitution and financing costs, net of each legally available recovery source; rerun the valuation with the shareholder-borne amount deducted or reflected in OE.

audit_findings.title: Wildfire Fund recovery could become a multibillion-dollar repayment obligation
audit_findings.magnitude: $645 million recorded Wildfire Fund receivable at 2026-06-30; $4.3 billion capped ceiling, equal to about $10.82 per share and 25%-33% of scenario equity value; uncapped case unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A reimbursement obligation would be a senior claim on equity through the bridge; associated unrecoverable borrowing costs would also reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: If the CPUC finds that SCE's conduct related to the ignition of the Eaton Fire was not prudent, SCE will be required to reimburse the Initial Account only for amounts disallowed by the CPUC up to the applicable Liability Cap of approximately $ 4.3 billion, unless the fund administrator finds that SCE's actions or inactions relative to the ignition of the Eaton Fire constitute conscious or willful disregard of the rights and safety of others, in which case SCE will be required to reimburse the Initial Account for withdrawn amounts that the CPUC disallowed .
audit_findings.explanation: No imprudence or willful-disregard determination has been demonstrated, so repayment is a contingent exposure rather than an established liability. Nevertheless, the filed $4.3 billion cap is large relative to equity values of $13.025-$17.102 billion, and the cap can disappear under the stated willful-disregard condition. The valuation contains no corresponding stress.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the fire-cause, SED, district-attorney and CPUC prudency evidence; track approved and paid Wildfire Fund reimbursements; rerun a current-withdrawal case, the $4.3 billion capped case and an explicitly unquantified uncapped case, including financing costs.

audit_findings.title: Accrual owner earnings may not represent distributable common cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $(3.445) billion regulatory-assets-and-liabilities cash flow in 2025 versus $1.219 billion inflow in 2024; the 2025 outflow was about 3.2 times the $1.0746 billion OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Regulatory revenue recognized before collection can inflate the OE anchor while omitted regulatory working-capital investment and collection delays reduce present distributable cash and increase financing needs.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash (used in)/provided by regulatory assets and liabilities, including changes in net over or undercollections recorded in balancing accounts, was $(3,445) million and $1,219 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a very large cash-timing mismatch, not a permanent $3.445 billion loss. Much of the 2025 movement arose from recognized settlement recoveries and other regulatory timing items, so a dollar-for-dollar valuation deduction is unsupported. Its scale relative to the anchor nevertheless makes the missing cash-conversion analysis reasonably capable of changing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to common-owner cash after changes in regulatory assets and liabilities; identify collectible amounts, expected collection dates, reasonableness-review exposure and financing costs; discount delayed recoveries and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Future Wildfire Fund contributions are not yet recorded
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.4 billion initial SCE share plus a possible $1.9 billion contingent share, or up to $4.3 billion nominal and undiscounted
audit_findings.mechanism: If triggered, unrecoverable shareholder contributions and borrowing costs would reduce future OE and potentially require an explicit liability or bridge adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: If the fund administrator determines contributions are required, the CPUC will extend the non-bypassable charge imposed under AB 1054 until January 1, 2046 to collect customer contributions for the Continuation Account of $9 billion, and the IOUs will be required to contribute an initial aggregate amount of $5.1 billion (SCE's share is $ 2.4 billion) over the period 2029 through 2045.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing states that the contribution trigger had not occurred, so this is a forward-looking obligation rather than a present model error. The nominal exposure is large, but its probability, timing and present value cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Monitor the fund administrator's depletion forecasts and contribution determination through 2028; if triggered or probable, schedule the 2029-2045 payments and any contingent installments, include unrecoverable borrowing costs, and rerun the DCF using their present value.

audit_findings.title: Static shares may not fund the capital plan
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed 2026-2030 capital expenditures are $37.5-$40.6 billion and the authorized capital structure includes 52% common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: External EIX common issuance would increase the share denominator; constrained funding could instead reduce achievable growth or increase financing costs within OE.
audit_findings.evidence: SCE needs substantial capital for its ongoing infrastructure investment program and for financing wildfire related losses.
audit_findings.explanation: The capital requirement is demonstrated, but future common issuance is not: retained earnings, debt, preferred capital, securitization and regulatory recoveries may fund part of the plan. The amount and price of any EIX issuance therefore remain unquantified and forward-looking.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a year-by-year sources-and-uses model covering retained OE, dividends, debt capacity, preferred financing, securitizations, wildfire cash needs and the 52% regulated equity requirement; rerun per-share value for any resulting issuance or growth shortfall.

audit_findings.title: The trend anchor may retain nonrecurring settlement benefits
audit_findings.magnitude: $414 million pre-tax 2025 interest-expense benefit ($171 million TKM plus $243 million Woolsey); exact OE and trend effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrepeatable reduction of interest expense can raise 2025 OE and, because 2025 is an endpoint in the log trend, raise the normalized OE anchor and all scenario values.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in SCE's core earnings in 2025 was primarily due to higher revenue from the 2025 GRC final decision and a benefit to interest expense related to cost recoveries authorized under the TKM and Woolsey Settlement Agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the $414 million settlement-related interest benefit, but the record does not establish how much survived the OE adjustments or what symmetrical normalization was applied to earlier wildfire losses and recoveries. The valuation effect therefore remains unresolved rather than demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2025 OE line by line, identify the after-tax portion of the TKM and Woolsey interest benefits retained, apply consistent normalization to historical wildfire losses and recoveries, and rerun the log-trend anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed upper stress: about $15.2 million, or 1.4%, added to the $1.0746 billion trend anchor; no more than about $0.60 per share across scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual proven to be eligible would be added back to historical OE, modestly raising the log-trend anchor and operating PV.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2016 $329.0m (15.7% of filed D&A); FY2018 $92.0m (4.7% of filed D&A); FY2019 $73.0m (4.0% of filed D&A); FY2021 $70.0m (3.1% of filed D&A); FY2022 $72.0m (2.7% of filed D&A); FY2024 $73.0m (2.5% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: Treating every listed residual as an eligible add-back—an aggressive upper stress—raises the computed trend anchor to about $1.0898 billion. The largest scenario increase is about $0.60 per share, leaving bull value near $43.64 versus the $56.77 market price and therefore not changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: No rerun is required for materiality; retain the conservative treatment unless filed component detail establishes eligibility, then update the historical OE schedule for completeness.
